author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: With the 2Y Treasury at 1.35% after a 43 bps 20-observation climb and the curve bear-flattening (10Y 1.96%, +61 bps, moderately steep) into the next US CPI print, markets are paying for cash return, pricing power and rate beneficiaries (banks, energy producers with buybacks, materials, Amgen/Peloton-style restructuring) and punishing duration and decelerating user-growth stories (Meta, PayPal, Spotify, REITs); the cross-currents are the ECB's pushback and Ukraine diplomacy in Europe, China easing into a soft patch with new US listing risk, and Poland's NBP hiking to a near nine-year high amid fiscal disarray and withheld EU funds.
sources_policy: Every fact comes from a headline in feeds/2022-02-09.json.gz (cited [[nNNNN]] in the same part) or from cards/2022-02-09.json (all sessions 2022-02-08; Treasury prior close 2022-02-08). No other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note was used as evidence. During setup a shared scratch file was overwritten by a parallel process and briefly displayed rows from other dates' cards; those values were discarded and every figure in the draft was re-read from the own-date card via tools/showcard.py into a private directory. Previews are used only as pending events; outcomes only from outcome headlines. Company news within 7 days, company results within 14, macro releases and policy baselines within 35. Each cited ID is used at most twice (267 distinct IDs). No numeric spot-FX; DXY only. Timing judgment: Commonwealth Bank's first-half result (n0069) is used because ASX pre-open releases on 9 February local time fall before 00:00 UTC; the card's CBA close (2022-02-08) is described as preceding the result. SoftBank's 2022-02-08 Tokyo close is described as preceding its results; no SoftBank results figures are claimed. Iran talks (n1442, n1453) are written as due to resume, not as an outcome.
known_ambiguities_omitted: US January CPI: no own-date preview gives a release date, so it is written as 'the next CPI print'/'the January CPI print' with no date and no outcome.
Disney, Uber and Toyota results: pending on 9 February with no own-date preview headline; not mentioned.
Chipotle fourth-quarter results (released after the 8 February US close): no own-date outcome headline; not discussed beyond its card close.

NBP Governor Glapiński's press conference: no own-date preview; referenced only generically via SII's 'NBP has not said its last word' (n1769). The size of the 8 February hike is not stated because only a pre-meeting preview (Pekao 50 bp, n1666) carries a number; it is used as a preview only.
SoftBank results: only a preview headline (n0842, Bloomberg 'set to show worsening') is available; no results figures used.
Pfizer intraday '4%' fall in n0834's headline: not quoted; the card close (-2.84%) is used instead.

Spot-FX headlines with numeric levels (n1589, n1590, n1591, n1631, n1632, n1685, and the EUR/USD item n1227): excluded under the spot-FX rule; only direction-free or qualitative currency references (n1286, n1272, n1775) are used.

Contradictory or opinion items on Russia-Ukraine: Defence24 opinion that there will be no invasion (n1669) and UNSW's 'war probably already underway' (n1397) were avoided as they contradict each other and the diplomatic-track reporting; the invasion is treated only as a pending risk.

Turów dispute claim/counter-claim (n1662: Morawiecki says money sent and complaint withdrawn, Prague says not): avoided as contradictory; EU fund withholding reported via DW/Guardian/NYT (n1545, n1546, n1547).

Promotional or forecast-hype items avoided: n0815 'Metaverse stocks to buy', n0501 Motley Fool '216% to 257%' hypergrowth, n0502 'cybersecurity stocks to buy', n0906 Fundstrat bitcoin $200k forecast, n0943 Bitcoin Magazine, n0642 Moomoo '50% profit within a day', n1174 minor-outlet claim that EU withdrawal would cost Facebook 25% of revenue.
Super Bowl items (n0927, n0941, n0945): the game is after the cutoff; only the pre-announced FTX giveaway plan is cited, with no outcome.
Stale-window company items avoided: Tesla record-earnings items stamped 26 January (n0958, n0960) and Seagate results (n0957) at the edge of the 14-day results window.
authoring_stage: initial nonretail draft before independent review
